Jordan / team,

I've attached the raw egress export for the time window you specified (egress-logs-20261102.csv) and a small patch showing the firewall/egress rule diff that was applied last week (egress-rule-diff.patch). Preliminary findings:

- Root cause: an automated deployment pipeline unintentionally rolled out an override to the egress policy on the production compute pool (rule ID egress-prod-override-2026-11-01). The override allowed outbound traffic to a third-party S3 endpoint used by one of our batch partners.
- Timeline (UTC):
  * 2026-11-01 22:03 — deployment job triggered (config change)
  * 2026-11-02 03:09 — first egress attempts observed
  * 2026-11-02 03:38 — automated alert (traffic spike)
  * 2026-11-02 03:45 — automated blocking rule reapplied; jobs restarted on corrected policy
  * 2026-11-02 04:10 — full containment verified
- Scope: outbound transfers were to a vendor-owned S3 bucket; no PII was identified in a cursory scan, but we will run a deeper content review and share results.

Actions taken:
- Reverted the misapplied policy and added an additional CI gate to prevent policy overrides without manual approval.
- Created JIRA ticket SEC-3421 for follow-up remediation items (retrospective, CI rule, and post-deploy validation).
- Generating signed hash of the exported CSV for chain-of-custody; hash file will be included in the SOC 2 bundle.

Attaching: egress-logs-20261102.csv, egress-rule-diff.patch

-Diego
Principal Engineer, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
